extracted.intended_audience: broadband industry stakeholders, utilities, FCC rulemaking participants, policymakers, and readers tracking broadband deployment policy
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes competing positions and concrete policy proposals submitted to the FCC on pole attachment rules — covering cost allocation, contractor access/timelines, invoice practices, make-ready work, and whether national standards or safety controls should govern. Useful for drafting or evaluating comments and rule options in the FCC proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard cost-cap (10% above estimate) for utilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a hard cap limiting utilities from billing more than 10 percent above their original estimate unless an attacher approves the additional cost in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed by INCOMPAS and Crown Castle to constrain overruns and improve predictability; justified by providers' claims of overruns of 200–300% and even 800% in some cases. Utilities (EEI) oppose "arbitrary cost caps," arguing field-condition variability drives costs and caps could incentivize inflated initial estimates or create unrecoverable costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final invoice issuance within 90 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Require utilities to issue final invoices within 90 days of completing work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requested by Crown Castle to avoid late billing that harms attachers' financial planning. The complaint notes attachers frequently receive invoices long after work is completed; utilities currently often do not itemize costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds within 60 days for make-ready overpayments
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachers should receive refunds within 60 days when they are required to perform make-ready payments themselves after utilities miss deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crown Castle's proposal to ensure attachers are not left out-of-pocket when utilities fail to meet timelines. Provides a specific time-bound remedy to delayed utility performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require itemized, timely cost transparency from utilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilities should itemize make-ready costs and provide invoices in a timely manner so attachers can predict expenses and plan deployments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCTA and other providers argue utilities frequently exceed estimates and do not itemize costs, undermining predictable planning. Lack of itemization and delayed billing are cited as major obstacles to BEAD deployments; transparency is presented as necessary for accountability and forecasting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit duplicative pre-application engineering charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify that utilities cannot assess multiple charges for the same preparatory work, and prevent duplicate preapplication engineering fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACA Connects reports some pre-application engineering studies cost up to $6,000 per deployment mile and may duplicate work already recovered through annual rental fees. The proposal asks the FCC to bar duplicate billing for identical preparatory tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm Section 224 covers utility-owned light poles (small-cell coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: FCC should confirm that Section 224 of the Communications Act covers utility-owned light poles to address high fees and restrictive terms that impede small-cell deployments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filed by CTIA to support wireless small-cell siting where traditional utility poles are unavailable; confirmation would extend Section 224 protections and potentially reduce fees/terms that block wireless deployments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set a 30-day cap on contractor approval/onboarding
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a 30-day limit as a reasonable time for utilities to approve contractors that attachers seek to use for standard tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCTA says some utilities take up to 20 months; a 30-day limit would prevent prolonged onboarding used to maintain exclusive control over timelines. Utilities counter that rapid mandatory onboarding could allow unqualified contractors and raise safety risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain utility control over contractor selection for safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow utilities to retain direct control over contractor selection and onboarding to enforce safety standards and prevent outages and accidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced by EEI and a coalition of multistate power companies opposing mandated contractor timelines; they argue that mandated onboarding could admit unqualified contractors into the power-supply space and that make-ready in the electric supply zone is complex and unsafe if simplified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not shift responsibility for preexisting third-party safety violations onto attachers
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilities should not require attachers to cover the full cost of replacing poles that have preexisting third-party safety violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comcast challenged Appalachian Power's policy that requires attachers to cover full replacement costs for poles with prior third-party safety violations (with limited reimbursement rules). Comcast argued such cost-shifting jeopardizes thousands of BEAD-funded deployments and asked the FCC to declare the policy unlawful under Section 224.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement rule when original violator relocates (50% rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: AEP's policy limits reimbursement to 50 percent only if the original violator relocates to the new pole; otherwise attachers may bear full replacement costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comcast criticized this reimbursement scheme as unlawful and harmful to deployments; utilities argue that attachers should not be permitted to shift responsibility for make-ready work involving safety violations. The dispute highlights allocation rules for costs when replacement is necessary due to prior violators.

rubrics_metrics.name: 120-day deadline for attachers to complete construction after make-ready
rubrics_metrics.description: Require attachers to complete construction within 120 days after make-ready is finished and notify utilities when work is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported by Dominion Energy and Xcel Energy to prevent attachers from leaving worksites in limbo; utilities say attachers often fail to notify completion, forcing utilities to dispatch personnel to verify builds. A fixed deadline is proposed to improve coordination and resource planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppose arbitrary cost caps due to field-condition variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid imposing rigid cost caps because make-ready cost variability is driven by field conditions and unforeseen engineering challenges, not utility mismanagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EEI and power-company coalitions warn that rigid caps could incentivize inflated initial estimates and create unrecoverable costs for utilities. This position argues for flexibility in cost recovery to reflect real-world conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not extend One-Touch Make-Ready (OTMR) into electric supply zone
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppose extending the Commission’s One-Touch Make-Ready rules to equipment located in the electric supply zone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Power companies and utilities argue "There is no such thing as simple make-ready in the power supply space," asserting that OTMR would be inappropriate and unsafe in those areas. This is a categorical safety/operational limitation on OTMR expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid new FCC regulation until existing rules are implemented
rubrics_metrics.description: The FCC should refrain from adopting additional pole-attachment regulations while earlier pole attachment rules are still being implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USTelecom cautions that layering more regulation during implementation could create confusion or counterproductive outcomes; recommends measured rollout and evaluation before new mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandate national standards for timelines, cost controls, and contractor access
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt uniform, national rules on timelines for approvals and construction, reasonable cost controls, and standardized contractor access procedures to ensure predictable, nationwide broadband deployments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported by some broadband providers and tower companies as a way to avoid state-by-state variance and accelerate BEAD-funded deployments. Utilities oppose national mandates arguing local field conditions, safety, and operational differences require flexibility.
